Maximum temperature difference in the tank floor during 30 minutes as a function of tank diameter. The structural analysis was performed on a flat floor, without accounting for initial deformation or residual stresses. This approach enables a direct comparison among multiple tanks having several diameters. Although this report presents a welding fabrication simulation to determine residual stress and initial floor distortion (Section 2.2) for 24 m and 32 m tank diameters, a more comprehensive analysis of stress evolution in the tank floor during operation is the subject of an upcoming publication. Stress contours on the tank floor developed during the charging operation are presented in Figure 11 for five tanks with different diameters and a flat floor 7 mm thick at the time stamps of 10, 20, and 30 minutes. This figure shows that the von Mises stress in the tank floor increases over time, particularly as the tank size increases. The maximum von Mises stress curves for different times and different tank diameters, considering three floor thicknesses—7 mm (baseline), 14 mm, and 21 mm—are presented in Figure 12.
